findings.what: hasClaims is hard-coded false in ToResponse, though Policy.HasClaims is stored and restored. No test seeds true, so a canned stub passes every hasClaims assertion.
findings.why: GET-1 returns the stored policy, and the F2 acceptance asks for the full response shape per api.md. Policy.HasClaims already exists end to end: PolicyRecord.HasClaims, PolicyRecordMapper.cs:21 into Policy.Restore, and PolicyRepository.cs:70. The comment says it is canned 'until F3 supplies the data', but that data is supplied today, so a canned stub value is left in green production code. The anti-oracle rule is broken too. PolicyResponseAssert.HasNoClaimsRefundsOrCancellation only ever expects false, and the Api.Tests PolicyBuilder passes a literal false to Restore with no override, so no test can tell the canned value from the stored one. A red test that seeds HasClaims=true and reads it back over HTTP must come before the mapping fix. Refunds, claims and cancellation have no domain data yet, so they are rightly canned.

findings.what: Header comment still says status and currentTermNumber are 'canned for now (stub step)'. At HEAD both come from PolicyDetails.Status and the current term's index.
findings.why: This is on the code-quality slop list: a comment that is false at HEAD. The refactor step fixed the same kind of stale comment on TwoDecimalPlacesConverter (7023420, 803c898) but missed this one. PolicyMappings.cs:23 already lists what is still canned.

findings.what: Global decimal converter writes with "F2", a silent second rounding path beside Money.Round. Its 'no >2 dp value reaches it' invariant lives only in a comment.
findings.why: CLAUDE.md says to round money only through Money.Round. At HEAD the invariant holds: the H6 400 rejects more than 2 dp by value before any 422 echo, and stored amounts come only from accepted sales. But F3's refunds will go through this converter, and "F2" formatting would hide a missing or wrong Money.Round (CANCEL-6) in every Api test. The change to problem echoes (-1e27 now written -1000000000000000000000000000.00) is consistent with the api.md money convention, but only gate.run evidences it. No Api test pins the echo's text, and the Postman decimal.MinValue test's include('"amount":-79228162514264337593543950335') is a prefix match that passes with or without '.00'.

findings.what: Known keys are every action parameter name, so ?reference= and ?cancellationToken= on GET (and ?request= on POST) pass without a 400, though no query value binds to them.
findings.why: The architecture skill says 'an unbound query key (case-insensitive) gives errors[key]', and requirements say an unknown query parameter returns 400. Route-bound, body-bound and special parameters are counted as known query keys. The only test is ?colour=red.
